title: Accelerating stencils on the Tenstorrent Grayskull RISC-V accelerator
problem: Stencil computations are computationally and energy-intensive on traditional CPUs. This work explores how to effectively map iterative stencil algorithms like Jacobi onto RISC-V based PCIe accelerators by optimizing for the Grayskull architecture's data movement and compute decoupling.
motivation: RISC-V based PCIe accelerators offer an alternative path to HPC acceleration that provides vendor flexibility while integrating into existing systems, bridging the gap until RISC-V CPUs mature in HPC.
method: The authors use the Jacobi iterative method as a stencil test case on the Tenstorrent Grayskull e150. They optimize code structure for the Grayskull's Tensix cores which decouple data movement from compute, then benchmark single and multi-accelerator configurations against Xeon Platinum CPUs in both performance and energy consumption.
key_novelty: RISC-V PCIe accelerators can achieve competitive stencil performance with 5x better energy efficiency compared to CPUs, demonstrating viability for HPC acceleration.
contributions: First evaluation of stencil kernels on Tenstorrent Grayskull RISC-V accelerator with best practices
Performance parity with Xeon Platinum CPU per e150 at BF16 precision
5x energy efficiency improvement per e150 over CPU baseline
Demonstrated 4x performance scaling with 4 e150s while maintaining 5x energy advantage

metrics.speedup: 4x with 4 e150s compared to single CPU; per-e150 performance matches Xeon Platinum
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 5x less energy consumption per e150; 5x less energy with 4 e150s

limitations: Generalization to other stencil algorithms and full FP32 precision comparison not discussed
